# 'stack restack' with a branch checked out in another worktree.
# The branch in the other worktree should be restacked there,
# not skipped.

as 'Test <test@example.com>'
at '2026-02-23T21:00:00Z'

mkdir repo
cd repo
git init
git commit --allow-empty -m 'Initial commit'
gs repo init

# Create a stack: main -> feature1 -> feature2 -> feature3

git add feature1.txt
gs bc feature1 -m 'Add feature1'
git add feature2.txt
gs bc feature2 -m 'Add feature2'
git add feature3.txt
gs bc feature3 -m 'Add feature3'

# Create a worktree for feature2.
git worktree add ../wt-feature2 feature2

# Move main to require restacking.
gs bco main
git add main-change.txt
git commit -m 'Change on main'

# Restack the stack from feature1.
gs bco feature1
gs stack restack

# feature2 should have been restacked in the other worktree.
stderr 'feature2: restacked in worktree'

# All branches should be restacked correctly.
git graph --branches
cmp stdout $WORK/golden/branches.txt

# Verify we're still on feature1.
git branch --show-current
stdout '^feature1$'

-- repo/feature1.txt --
feature1

-- repo/feature2.txt --
feature2

-- repo/feature3.txt --
feature3

-- repo/main-change.txt --
main change

-- golden/branches.txt --
* 973316c (feature3) Add feature3
* 7f032ba (feature2) Add feature2
* a62abc9 (HEAD -> feature1) Add feature1
* 966cc06 (main) Change on main
* e2e096d Initial commit
